result.process_description:
Title: Ordering in an Online Shop  

A customer that logs into an E-Shop system and has to wait for its login confirmation (its credentials are checked by the system).
If the login was successful then the customer can continue to select products, else the shopping experience stops.
After selecting a product the customer has to add it to a shopping cart, save the product and check if every product was already selected.
These steps repeat until all products were selected.
Then the order is finished by the shopping system and simultaneously payment and shipment for the order is prepared.
For the payment the customer has to enter its payment data and has to wait until the bank confirms the payment.
While waiting for the payment confirmation the customer can enter its shipping address (an independent billing address can be entered if the shipping address is not equal to the billing address).
Finally if the address and the payment steps are executed then the order will be finished by the system.

result.rule: Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
Sequence flows may cross lanes in one process. Use message flows across participant pools, never between lanes.

result.rule: When the description says the process waits for a response from an outside party or group, or until a period of time or a later point in time has passed, whichever comes first, before it continues to a decision or the next step: Model the wait as an event-based gateway. Give one branch an intermediate message catch event for the expected response. Give the other branch an intermediate timer catch event for the stated duration or point in time. Place any step the description ties to the timeout (for example, escalating or forwarding) after the timer event. Do not model the wait as an extra task or as sequential catch events, because the description states a race between the two outcomes.

When the description says that a question is put to a participant and that the answer decides which of two alternative sequences of later steps follows: Model the question as an activity performed before the decision. Place an exclusive gateway directly after it, with one conditional outgoing sequence flow per possible answer, and give each alternative its own branch of steps. Join the alternative branches with an exclusive gateway before the next step that all paths share. Do not place the alternative steps in one unconditional sequence, and do not omit the gateway that makes the answer-based choice explicit.

When the description makes a decision (a gateway) that depends on the replies or agreement of several invited people, so the flow cannot continue until those replies are in: Before the decision gateway, model an intermediate catch event that waits for the replies from the people concerned, so the decision is taken only after the responses arrive. Keep the decision gateway and any loop back to the earlier activity as the description states them.

When the description states that a participant itself receives or confirms the result of a step, and a next action follows directly after it, with no stated waiting time and no external message or condition the process waits for: Model that result as a task carried out by the participant, placed in the sequence before the next action. Use an intermediate catch event or an event-based gateway only when the description states that the process waits for an external message, signal, time or condition.
